newsitem.title: UK: TR European says KEPIT cash deal poor.
newsitem.headline: TR European says KEPIT cash deal poor.

text.p: Proposals from the Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust Plc to offer investors a choice between opting for cash, continuing investment in European privatisation or a general Europe unit trust will be bad for shareholders, advisers to hostile bidders for KEPIT said.

"What KEPIT is doing is loading all the costs of the transaction onto those investors who opt for cash," Rolly Crawford, joint head of investment trusts at ABN Amro Hoare Govett, which is advising TR European on its hostile bid for KEPIT.

"What will happen under the terms of their cash offer is that those who choose cash will be left with the dregs of a portfolio that nobody wants," said James de Sausmarez, managing director of retail fund management at Henderson Administration.

Shane Ross, chairman of the independent board of KEPIT that under the M&G and Kleinwort Benson proposals, some of KEPIT's assets would be transferred to the two trusts without incurring dealing costs which liquidation of KEPIT would cause.
"Investors will get 107.4 pence per share under our offer if all of them opted for cash. If the board believes that they can do better than that, then why do they not say so," Crawford said.

On Tuesday, KEPIT recommended shareholders opt for proposals from M&G and Kleinwort Benson Investment Management to choose between units in the Kleinwort Benson European Privatisation Trust, units in an existing European unit trust, the M&G European and General Fund, or units in the Kleinwort Benson Money Market Trust, which can be held as an investment or redeemed to provide cash.

"M&G have identified approximately one third of KEPIT's securities which M&G European would be prepared to retain and KBIM and M&G have agreed how, depending on the level of elections for M&G Euro, a corresponding portion of these assets can be transferred to M&G European without KEPIT incurring dealing costs while protecting the interest of all KEPIT investors," Ross said.
However, TR European attacked the performance of both M&G's fund and of Kleinwort Benson Investment Management.
"We know all about KBIM's performance from the poor performance of KEPIT," said Crawford.
He also noted the performance of TR European had been markedly superior to that of the M&G general European fund.
"Over the past six months, their performance with income reinvested has been up 1.3 percent, up 7.3 percent over 12 months and up 89.7 percent over five years," Crawford said.
TR European has returned 19.8 percent over six months, 28.4 percent over 12 months and 148.0 percent over five years, without income reinvested.
"If you look at the alternative investment vehicles, there is no reason to believe that the managers can be more succesful than in the past," Crawford.
"In terms of a rollover vehicle for investments, TR European is an awful lot better than any of the alternatives," said Crawford.
"I am surprised that M&G is prepared to let the whole world see how poor its performance is in comparison with the alternative," he added.
